region.text: Gaulanitis, Trachonitis, Batanaea, Auranitis and Paneas/Iturea

ledger.note: 4 BCE: Philip becomes tetrarch of the north. 'Philip became tetrarch of the northern territories, including Gaulanitis, Trachonitis, Batanaea, Auranitis, and Paneas/Iturea, with Caesarea Philippi as his capital'; 'he maintained his rule from Herod's death in 4 BCE until his own in 34 CE' (Philip page).
4 BCE: the tetrarchy is a Roman client from Augustus's confirmation of Herod's will ('Augustus largely confirmed the division of territory set out by Herod in his final will').

34: Philip dies and Rome takes the tetrarchy. 'Philip ruled over territories north and east of the Jordan River until 34 CE'; his lands were briefly added to the province of Syria (the page's wording, as WebFetch reported it).
34: the tetrarchy is added to the province of Syria. 'Philip ruled over territories north and east of the Jordan River until 34 CE'; his lands were briefly added to the province of Syria.

34: Philip dies and the tetrarchy ends (the Philip page: 'until his own [rule] in 34 CE', infobox 'Died: 34 AD'; 'Vacant Title next held by King Agrippa I'). Agrippa I receives the lands in 37 (Herodian tetrarchy page).

certainty.note: No page gives the tetrarchy's boundaries; Golan and Hauran stand for the six districts.

notes: Two pages (budget 2-5, no Cliopatria shapes). No war moved Philip's border on the pages. The 37 grant to Agrippa I is on the Herodian tetrarchy page; kingdom-of-herod-agrippa-i is written in this batch and takes the 37 grant. The six districts (Iturea, Trachonitis, Batanea, Paneas, Gaulanitis, Auranitis) are named by the pages; the gazetteer has only Golan (Gaulanitis) and Hauran (Auranitis), which stand in for the whole. The Philip page lists 'a certain part of what is called the House of Zenodorus' among his lands (Zenodorus's old principality, see itureans). Gazetteer names wanted: Iturea, Trachonitis, Batanea, Paneas, Peraea.
